items.title: Cannot separate development from human rights and dignity: Former CJI BR Gavai
items.summary: Human rights cannot be separated from questions of social and economic development, former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai said on Friday. Justice Gavai examined the deep connection between fundamental freedoms and sustainable development goals. “A person may formally possess political liberty, but the substantive value of that liberty is diminished when that person is deprived of food, education, healthcare, livelihood, or the basic conditions necessary for living a life with human dignity. Rights therefore cannot exist merely as abstractions,” the former judge said. He was delivering the ninth Chief Justice MC Chagla Memorial Lecture. He stressed that economic growth by itself is insufficient to measure human progress. “When we speak of development, who the development is for, development towards what end, and development at whose cost?" he asked. Justice Gavai recalled his experience presiding over the Supreme Court's Green Bench. He described judicial decision-making as "walking the tightrope for balancing between ecology and environment on one hand and sustainable development on the other hand." items.title: Yogesh Gowda murder case: Karnataka High Court suspends life sentence of seven convicts
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday (September 18) suspended the life sentences imposed on seven persons convicted by a trial court for the 2016 murder of BJP leader and Dharwad Zilla Panchayat member Yogesh Gowda, holding that they were entitled to be released on bail pending disposal of their criminal appeals. A Division Bench of Justice Mohammad Nawaz and Justice G Basavaraja passed the order on applications filed by the seven convicts (appellants) as part of their appeal challenging the trial court verdict. The Court also imposed various conditions for their release on bail. The appellants have been directed to execute a bond for ₹5 lakh each, along with two sureties for the like sum. They were also directed to deposit the entire fine amount imposed on them by the trial court, not leave India without the prior permission of the High Court and appear before the High Court or trial court whenever directed. The only other records of Demoiselle Crane sighting from Tamil Nadu comes from Vijayanarayanam Tank in Tirunelveli. Naman Bora and Amoggh Chatty found the vagrant bird feeding in the reeds at Nemmeli salt pans near Chennai; the former would return to the spot the next three days and find the bird tenaciously clinging to this feeding spot
